subject: Emotions
title: The Orienting Response
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Orienting Response.

hook.text: A strange noise in the forest. Every animal freezes and turns toward it. Pavlov called this 'What is it?'

buildup.text: The orienting response is automatic: heart rate slows, pupils dilate, and attention locks onto the novel stimulus.

discovery.text: TV ads use scene cuts every few seconds to keep triggering your orienting response. You can't look away.

twist.text: The response is metabolically expensive. Too many novel stimuli cause mental fatigue—the cost of modern life.

climax.text: Meditation trains the brain to notice the orienting response without following it. Awareness without capture.

punchline.text: Your attention is a reflex. Surprise pulls the trigger.
